nws.synopsis: Cooling will spread inland into the weekend with high temperatures on Sunday around 10 to 15 degrees below average for inland areas. Chances for showers will begin increasing on Friday and be highest during the weekend. There remains a fairly wide spread in potential rainfall with around a 50 percent chance of 0.50 inch or less from the coast to the mountains with a 15 to 20 percent chance for 2 inches or more. Tides will remain elevated through much of this week with near record water levels resulting in coastal flooding.

sites.name: Torrey Pines
sites.note: Ridge soaring in a steady W to WNW sea breeze. SW or NW is cross (soarable but not great); only east is over the back. Rare thermal days (1,200 ft+) are flagged as a Thermal day.

sites.name: Little Black
sites.note: Best post-frontal site in the county. West-facing, so offshore mornings are over the back.

sites.name: Blossom Valley
sites.note: Inland thermal site; often lines up with Elsinore.

sites.name: Elsinore
sites.note: East-facing over the lake; its own animal. Launch in the light air before the switch; the west wind then builds the convergence inland (Perris, Hemet, Soboba). XC wants 7-8k over the range during the switch and the same or more inland.

sites.name: Soboba
sites.note: Flight park on the San Jacinto front.

sites.name: Otay Mesa
sites.note: Near the border; XC goes north and east.

sites.name: Laguna / Horse
sites.note: Two launches: Horse faces west, Laguna faces east over the desert. Each is scored on its own and the better one is shown.

sites.name: Santa Barbara (Skyport)
sites.note: South-facing front range above Santa Barbara; launch sits above the marine layer, so thermals are measured from the slopes at launch height. Sundowners and other real north winds are over the back.

sites.name: Owens Valley (Walt's Point)
sites.note: Watch only: shows when it rates 5. Advanced pilots only. Morning site with very strong thermals, cloudbase 13-20k. Needs light winds; west wind over the Sierra is a no-go. PGs don't fly it June to early September.
